sam: Heads-up — saw a sharp perf cliff in mixed-precision routing during a 3k+ token prefill workload. TPS drops ~45% when FP8 decode path is chosen and KV eviction kicks in. Logs attached below.

anya: hmm, is this the same regression we saw after the dequant hotpath PR? which flag did you toggle?

sam: I repro'd on staging with `DEQUANT_EAGER=1` off (so lazy deq) and `adaptive_kernel_select=true`. Short runs (<1k) look fine: prefill ~6ms/token, decode ~18ms/token. Long run (3k) decode jumps to ~65ms/token after ~1.8k tokens and stays high.

devon: interesting — could be KV-shard eviction thrashing the microbatch scheduler. When the working set exceeds a shard boundary we spill and the dequant path loops more. Can you paste the perf counters?

sam: pasted below (from perfbot profiler):
```
PROFILE SNAPSHOT: 2026-03-18 14:12:01
seq_len=3200, batch=4
- total_tokens_prefill: 12800
- kernel_select: FP8_prefill -> INT8_decode fallback at token=1824
- avg_prefill_ms_per_token: 5.9
- avg_decode_ms_per_token (0..1823): 17.6
- avg_decode_ms_per_token (1824..3200): 64.8
- KV_evictions/sec: 12.4 (spike at 1820)
- GPU_util_post_eviction: drop 72% -> 38%
```

anya: that kernel switch at 1824 is suspect — is it a manual fallback (capacity-based) or automatic mismatch due to quant calib confidence?

perfbot: detected: "kernel-mismatch-on-kv-boundary". Recent builds: runtime@v1.23.4. Correlated with calib sampler change in runtime commit c3f9.

marta: we shipped a small change to the calibration sampler that biases toward smaller quant ranges for attention KV tables to reduce noise. Could that change the runtime's compatibility matrix and force a decode fallback when combined with the shard alignment?

devon: yes — if the compile-time kernel selection table reports an incompatible kernel for the decode path, the runtime currently falls back to a slower dequant->float->kernel path instead of using a hybrid decode kernel. On long contexts the number of such fallbacks accumulates and multiplies latency because of KV eviction churn.

sam: repro experiment: pinned compatibility table to previous version (runtime@v1.23.2) and reran. No cliff; decode stayed ~18ms/token. So two interacting factors: calibration sampler tweak + KV eviction threshold crossing.

anya: good find. Proposed fixes: (1) add an early compatibility check that prefers hybrid decode kernels over full fallback, (2) shift KV eviction hysteresis to avoid crossing shard boundary mid-request, (3) instrument a per-request kernel-selection histogram so we can detect boundary-triggered flips. Thoughts?

devon: agreed. Also we should add a microbenchmark that simulates long-context microbatch sequences with aligned shard offsets, run it across quant variants: FP8/INT8/4bit. If hybrid kernel latency is within 1.2x of ideal, prefer it.

marta: I'll revert the calibration sampler tweak on an experimental branch and run a 48h soak with the microbenchmark. Can someone add the per-request histogram to the telemetry?

anya: I can add histograms. Suggest tags: model_name, kernel_path, kv_shard_offset, seq_len_bucket. Keep cardinality low.

perfbot: telemetry change request created: PERF-4283. Microbenchmark job queued (queue: longctx-quant-soak).

sam: quick mitigation for prod: for requests with seq_len > 1500 set `kernel_selector.prefer_hybrid=true` and bump eviction hysteresis by 1 shard. We can toggle via feature flag.

infra-bot: Feature flag `hybrid_prefer_longctx` created (rollout: 0% -> 50% over 30m) by marta.

devon: follow-ups: (a) add compile-time fallback that emits a lightweight hybrid decode kernel, (b) audit other calibration changes that may shift compatibility, (c) run the microbenchmark matrix for FP8/INT8/4bit and report perf/regression deltas. I'll own (a).

sam: thanks — I'll monitor the rollout and capture traces if cliff reappears. If anyone wants the repro script: `./scripts/longctx_quant_repro.sh --seq 3200 --batch 4 --calib-variant new`

marta: adding to the eng-runtime runbook: note about kernel flips on shard boundaries and the runtime flag to prefer hybrid kernels.

anya: nice catch, team. :thumbsup:

sam: ending note — this one was a classic interaction bug (quant calibration x eviction x kernel selection). worth a short doc for P0 triage next time.
